correctness.rationale: With coupling K per neighbor, equilibrium forces constant sine on each parity and their odd-minus-even difference is a/K. The signed cycle form is evaluated on exactly the zero-sum space of edge differences. Two negatives, or a negative and a zero, are excluded by equal opposite edge differences. Against a single conductance −c, the other m−1 edges of that parity have +c; taking differences 1 on the negative edge and −1/(m−1) on those gives −c+c/(m−1)<0. Vanishing conductances alone delete an entire parity and create extra zero modes. Thus strict stability requires acute increments. The winding condition and monotone sine difference for d∈(0,π−|2πq/m|) give precisely one labelled phase class per q with 2|q|<m and K>K_q, excluding threshold equality. The Fourier blocks give both spectral bands; all minus modes lie at or below −(u+v), and r=1,m−1 in the plus band gives the slowest nonzero rate. At q=0 both conductances equal sqrt(K²−a²/4); at nonzero q the weak conductance is aε/sin(2π|q|/m)+O(ε²) while the other stays positive. Expanding the exact full gap yields the stated coefficients, powers and remainder orders, with fixed m,q,a. Winding signs interchange the two conductances.
residual_risks: The uploaded script was inspected, not run. Its 630 recorded spectrum/residual comparisons are finite; the gap tests sample one small offset at six ring sizes. The illustrative path-weight loop (lines 63–68) has one more positive entry than a 2m-cycle with one deleted edge, so it is not an exact path reconstruction; the corrected proof gives the exact zero-sum witness directly. No nonlinear stability at threshold is inferred.

evidence: The signed-cycle test with nonzero conductances requires all positive, or one negative and negative reciprocal sum. For one negative −c, equal sine within its parity gives at least m−1 positive +c entries, making the reciprocal sum positive. Thus the stability exclusion is a direct specialization and is credited, including the negative-edge possibility in other general rings.
The inspected cycle-flow and inertia statements do not establish magnitudes of the smallest nonzero eigenvalues or a rate as K approaches each winding threshold.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Inertia alone cannot tell how fast the transverse eigenvalues collapse. The full acoustic band must be compared across Fourier modes, and the detuning equations distinguish vanishing of both conductances from vanishing of only one.

At central onset the Jacobian itself vanishes and all conductances are of order √ε. At a noncentral onset m isolated dimers remain and m−1 additional relative modes soften; the full least decay coefficient comes from the r=1,m−1 plus band together with the exact derivative of the small conductance. These numbers do not follow from signs, branch type or local threshold alone.

value.rationale: Two different critical slowing-down rates occur on stable branches of the same homogeneous cycle with the same detuning pattern. The exact winding and size dependence of the slowest transverse time scale distinguishes all-link collapse from weak links between surviving dimers, even in the presence of multiple vanishing modes at a threshold. The full-space coefficient is useful for estimating the slow approach of perturbations and is not given by a reduced stability exchange. Standard Fourier band formulas or the already-covered branch count alone are not the basis of this value judgment.
residual_risks: Does not quantify nonlinear relaxation times, basin geometry, or simultaneous large-ring limits.
